vectors.desc: struct field order bytewise case-sensitive: 'A' sorts before 'a'
deriv: the sort key is the raw field-name byte sequence, case-sensitive: 'A' (41) sorts before 'a' (61) — no locale, case, or collation folding; a declaration order of {a, A} never leaks into the table (WF-22 :668-674; VS-6)
value body follows the sorted table: A=1 (22), a=2 (24); canonicalization never reorders structure except maps (KO-6 :1086-1098)
c4 DD r2: repeat type-ref intern id corrected — DESC INT is id 2 (DFS: struct 0, 'A' 1, int 2, 'a' 3); REF d2, not d3 (WF-22)

vectors.desc: KO-1 base order: string key skeletons compare bytewise, case-sensitive
deriv: envelope (c4 DD r5): root DESC E0 D5 (STRING id 1, INT-8 id 2) — root DESC MAP: E0 D5, key type-ref, elem type-ref, in this order (WF-22 :620)
keys 'B' and 'a': skeletons are length-prefixed STRING literals, never REF tokens — 01 42 < 01 61 bytewise; the pair sort precedes emission (KO-1 :1021-1029; KO-6 :1086-1090)
emission is independent of the in-memory map's iteration order; 'a' declared or inserted first never reorders the bytes (KO-2 :1032-1041)

vectors.desc: KO-2b value-bytes tie-break: byte-equal pointer-key skeletons, distinct values
deriv: envelope (c4 DD r5): root DESC per-value: value 1 = DESC POINTER over DESC BOOL (ids 0/1) + body — the cell opens as an addressable record (id 2); value 2 = type repeat REF d0 + body (cell id 3); value 3 = DESC MAP E0 D5, key type-ref REF d0 (the pointer desc), elem type-ref DESC INT-8 (id 4) — the ambient framing of SENSOR-2 item 3 is superseded (WF-22 :617, :620; WF-24 :745-753)
two distinct *bool cells open as values 1-2 (records 2/3) under DESC POINTER(BOOL), tag elided at grain equality, bodies 11 11; the map keys are REFs d2/d3 (WF-24 :840-846; derivA2 SENSOR-2 item 3)
skeletons collapse reference-kind components to the nil token — both keys skeleton to 00, byte-equal across distinct identity slots (E2 :1005-1008; KO-2 :1032-1041)
KO-2b orders the tied pairs by the canonical bytes of the pair VALUE: 22 < 24 — deterministic and value-derived, never consulting implementation-run identity (KO-2b :1042-1048)

vectors.desc: T2 tied-pair fixture: byte-equal skeleton and value bytes, Go-declared order
deriv: envelope (c4 DD r5): root DESC per-value: as V-104 — cells id 2/3, the map's key type-ref REF d0, elem DESC INT-8 id 4 (WF-22 :617, :620)

two distinct *bool slots, byte-equal key skeletons (E2 collapse) AND byte-equal value bytes 28 0E — the pair order is E5/KO-2a territory: an identity-sequence discriminator over the tie-break identity determinant that never enters the encoded bytes (KO-2a :1049-1061; E5 :1010-1013)
this fixture pins the go binding's declared tier-2 instantiation — registration order (d2 before d3) as the identity sequence (KO-2a)

the value is OUTSIDE the stable class — no map anywhere may apply the E5 tie-break — so cross-language byte equality is not claimed; within the declared scope the tier-2 encoding agrees across machines, and the decode-side canonicality rejects hold in every tier (tier ladder :940-960; stable class :1118-1124)

vectors.desc: KO-4 interface keys: the dynamic-type tag is part of the key bytes
deriv: envelope (c4 DD r5): root DESC E0 D5 — MAP(INTERFACE, INT-8): key type-ref DESC INTERFACE E0 D8 08 (id 1), elem DESC INT-8 (id 2); the interface keys carry their dynamic-type DESC literals inside the map body (WF-22 :620, :623; KO-4)

a key encoding of an interface is (dynamic-type tag, canonical value): int32(1) and int64(1) are different keys — the DESC literals e0 d8 0a 04 and e0 d8 0a 08 differ in the width byte, and the skeleton compares the tag bytes bytewise: 04 < 08 (KO-4 :1072-1077)
a nil interface key and a typed-nil key are byte-distinct — the bare nil token against a dynamic descriptor plus nil body (KO-4 :1077-1079; V-94)
c4 DD r2: width-8 argument re-spelled on the WF-7 ladder — u8 rung 08 08 (inline caps at 7; the (01/02/04/08) parenthetical WF-22 :638 is a pre-rebalance residue; 16 remains 08 10)
c4 DD r2: pair bodies completed — key1=int32(1) desc+22, value1=22, key2=int64(1) desc+22, value2=24; the round-1 bytes dropped value1 and mislabeled key2's image (KO-4)

vectors.desc: KO-8 skip path: byte-identical key token sequences rejected
deriv: envelope (c4 DD r5): root DESC per-value: value 1 = DESC ARRAY[2] INT-8 (ids 0/1, backing id 2); value 2 = DESC MAP(SLICE INT-8, BOOL) — SLICE id 4 elem REF d1, BOOL id 5 — would-be prefix before the duplicate keys (WF-22 :618, :620)
one backing [1,2] (82 02 22 24, id 2); both keys spell the identical view token sequence 91 02 00 01 — off 0 len 1 extent 1 over the same record (WF-17 :484, :494-499)

the two windows materialize the same one-element slice: byte-equal skeletons of pointer-free key kinds are true duplicates — on the skip path byte-identical key token sequences are a decoder reject; a duplicate is always an attack or corruption (KO-8 :1104-1112; E1 :998-1001; WF-18 :517-519)

vectors.desc: struct field table emitted out of name-sorted order rejected
deriv: field table [b, a]: the second field name 'a' (61 61) sorts before 'b' — the descriptor's field table is emitted in canonical name-sorted order and a table in any other order is a decoder reject of class field_table_unsorted; the prefix halts at the out-of-order name (WF-22 :668-676, c4 pin P2)
canonical spelling sorts the table [a, b] and the value body follows it

vectors.desc: ESC reserved nibble nonzero rejected: one legal spelling per token
deriv: token f1: the low nibble of an ESC first byte is reserved — an emitter MUST write zero (F0), a decoder MUST reject a nonzero nibble; a second legal spelling of one token would break the one-legal-byte-sequence contract the moment a subclass graduates (WF-23 :720-726)
the same reservation governs the argumentless class bytes 40/50/B0/E0; this reject is a canonicality class, tier-invariant (WF-23 :726-734; WF-25 :923-935)

vectors.desc: KO-6 struct keys: blank fields neither encode nor compare
deriv: envelope (c4 DD r5): the root DESC is the MAP — E0 D5, key type-ref = the struct DESC nested (E0 D0 01 'x' DESC INT-8, ids 1..3), elem type-ref REF d3 (INT-8, hash-consed); the framing desc folds into the root's descriptor (WF-22 :620, :654-660)
the MAP's key type-ref nests {_, x: INT-8} — a blank field declared — blank fields are not part of the descriptor and are not encoded: the table holds x only (WF-19 :541-546; WF-22 :674)
the key skeleton is the struct's canonical encoding with fields strictly in table order — b0 26; blank fields neither encode nor compare (KO-6 :1086-1098)

vectors.desc: KO-3 float key: -0.0 encoded as-is, never normalized
deriv: envelope (c4 DD r5): the root DESC is the MAP — E0 D5, key type-ref DESC FLOAT-32 (id 1), elem type-ref DESC INT-8 (id 2); the framing desc folds into the root's descriptor (WF-22 :620, :626-631)

key type FLOAT-32 as the MAP's nested type-ref E0 D8 0C 04 (WF-22 :610-616, :627-631); the key is the raw bits 80000000 big-endian at type width — the encoder never normalizes +-0 in any position; the stored representation is observable and round-trips bit-for-bit (KO-3 :1063-1069)

E4: at most one zero float key of a given type may occupy the map — this sole -0.0 slot is legal; which sign a collapsed zero slot stores is the zero-sign determinant, tier-2 instantiable and excluded from the tier-1 claim (E4 :1008-1010; tier ladder :940-960)

vectors.desc: KO-8 materialized collapse: same identity slot twice, pair count != slot count
deriv: envelope (c4 DD r5): root DESC per-value: value 1 = DESC BOOL (id 0) + body — the cell (record id 1); value 2 = DESC MAP(POINTER(BOOL), INT-8): key type-ref DESC POINTER (id 3) target REF d0, elem DESC INT-8 (id 4) — would-be bytes (WF-22 :617, :620)
one bool cell (record id 1 behind DESC BOOL id 0, body 11); both map keys are REF d1 — the same identity slot named twice, not two byte-equal distinct slots (V-104/V-105) (WF-24 :768-782)

pointer-carrying keys collapse at value-model insertion: pair count 2 != final slot count 1 -> reject — key encodings equal including the identity layer are a decoder reject, always an attack or corruption (KO-8 :1104-1112)

vectors.desc: ESC F0 with subclass 7f: unknown subclass in version 2
deriv: envelope: root DESC BOOL E0 D8 09 (WF-22 :628); the known value position carries ESC token f0 7f

the ESC low nibble is reserved zero — f0 (WF-23 :764-766); the second byte 7f sits in the experimental range 00..7f (:768-769) and version 00 02 assigns no subclass anywhere — an unknown subclass is a format error (:769-770)
complements V-109 (nonzero reserved nibble f1); the canonicality family is tier-invariant — the decode-side contract holds in every tier (WF-25 :995-996)
